top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice removes the trapping-light shift on the clock transition, enabling many-atom interrogation and 10^-18 stability and accuracy, reproduced independently at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB and SYRTE, and opening laboratory tests of gravitational redshift, constants and dark matter. The credit to Katori (proposal and first lattice clock) and Ye (systematics and stability to the limit) is clean and the work is mature. The residual doubt about lineage after the 2005 and 2012 prizes does not outweigh this, so an award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Loose scientific acquaintance only: I spent a year in John Hall's laboratory at JILA during my PhD, and Jun Ye works in that environment; no collaboration with Katori or Ye apparent from profile. No recusal-requiring conflict.
